comparison: Both strongly support the dual recombinase system methodology (MCIR and IR1). OpenEval emphasizes the detailed genetic constructs and sound experimental design (C6, C7, C39, C50-C55), while peer reviewers describe it as 'compelling' and 'convincing' with successful mapping capabilities. Complete agreement on methodological strength.

Perfect alignment on IR1 system findings showing tissue-specific hierarchical relationships (C103-C108, C126-C127). Both accept the PDL hierarchy and absence of clear hierarchy in pulp. OpenEval provides detailed methodological justification while peer reviewers affirm the hierarchical relations as valid findings.

Both support the ablation experiment findings (C109-C112). OpenEval notes appropriate experimental design but mentions lack of quantification and rescue experiments as limitations. Peer reviewers accept the functional data without raising concerns, stating methods and data support the claims.

Complete agreement on PDGFR-α+ cell heterogeneity findings (C113-C114). OpenEval notes appropriate marker use but mentions lack of quantification and functional characterization. Peer reviewers accept the immunofluorescence findings without objection as part of comprehensive characterization.

Both support tissue clearing methodology and distribution findings (C56-C64, C69-C71, C87-C88, C102). OpenEval emphasizes honest acknowledgment of significant limitations (poor tdTomato signal, autofluorescence). Peer reviewers treat these limitations as methodological transparency rather than fundamental flaws, accepting the comprehensive mapping effort.

OpenEval supports distribution patterns from tissue clearing (C61-C64) with convergent evidence from multiple methods. Peer R2 accepts these distribution findings as part of comprehensive mapping. Both view the multi-method approach positively despite acknowledged limitations.

Both support lineage tracing findings. OpenEval emphasizes quantitative rigor (2.19-fold change, C85-C86) and consistency across methods (C91-C94). Peer reviewers explicitly affirm capacity for progeny cell generation (C120, C123-C124) without concerns about the data.

OpenEval supports serial sectioning advantages and limitations (C72-C79, C95-C97), noting superior tdTomato detection but z-axis discontinuities. Peer R3 affirms the complementary approach using tissue clearing and 3D reconstruction (C73-C97), treating multiple methods as strengthening conclusions.

OpenEval supports DICOM-3D reconstruction as methodological triangulation (C80-C82). Peer R3 affirms the complementary approach of multiple reconstruction methods, viewing it as strengthening rather than undermining conclusions.

Both support tissue-specific differences in cell behavior (C118-C125). OpenEval notes reasonable inference about niche-specific roles but states regenerative function speculation requires validation. Peer reviewers accept tissue-specific differences as valid findings from the MCIR system.

Overlapping support for lineage tracing capacity findings. OpenEval R9 synthesizes MCIR findings across tissues (C118-C125), while Peer R4 explicitly affirms progeny cell generation capacity (C120, C123-C124). Both accept the tissue-specific behavioral differences.

OpenEval rates cranial findings as UNCERTAIN, noting speculation about MSC function in cranial sutures lacks functional evidence (C98-C101). Peer R8 accepts cranial mapping data without challenge, with anonymous reviewer stating methods and data support claims. Divergence in confidence level.

OpenEval's UNCERTAIN rating for NFATc1+ cell distribution in alveolar bone (C69-C70) contrasts with Peer R2's acceptance of comprehensive mapping. OpenEval notes tissue clearing limitations may affect reliability; peer reviewers view limitations as transparency rather than undermining findings.

Both support the summary conclusion about system capabilities (C115). OpenEval emphasizes extensive experimental validation across multiple tissues and methods. Peer reviewers affirm the spatiotemporal atlas generation and comprehensive mapping achievements.

Both support the dual imaging approach evaluation (C38, C41). OpenEval values the comparative analysis and scientific rigor in acknowledging limitations. Peer reviewers implicitly accept methodological reflection, noting limitations don't undermine overall conclusions.

Both strongly support overarching findings (C9-C10, C40). OpenEval cites extensive imaging, lineage tracing, and hierarchical analysis as robust support. Peer reviewers affirm the comprehensive mapping and characterization, describing work as 'compelling' and methods supporting claims.

Both support acknowledgment of methodological limitations (C128-C130). OpenEval notes this critical self-assessment is appropriate but 'somewhat undermines confidence in current results.' Peer reviewers view adequately discussed limitations as not undermining conclusions, maintaining positive overall assessment.
